subject: Production latency spike: 429/5xx surge and retry amplification
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara@brightcart.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden spike in 429/5xx across 11:30-11:50 PT

Jonas —

We're seeing a production incident affecting our API integrations with Redwood between ~11:30–11:50 PT. Clients are seeing a ton of 429s and intermittent 5xxs. Latency climbed from ~120ms to 2–3s and appears to then timeout. Retries from our side are amplifying traffic and we can see token-level failures in the Redwood responses.

This is impacting checkout flows for several of our enterprise customers. Our engineering team captured traces showing many aborted handshakes to redwood-inference-us-west-2 and repeated DNS lookup failures for the primary resolver.

Can you confirm if there's any known outage on your end? We need an ETA for a mitigation path — even a temporary region reroute or an emergency rollback to a different model variant would help.

Attached: sample-traces-11-30.json (small), brief-stats.csv

Thanks,
Sara
S. Li
Head of Ops, BrightCart

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden spike in 429/5xx across 11:30-11:50 PT

Sara —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the traces. I'm escalating this immediately to our on-call infra and CS leads. We're treating this as a priority incident and will keep you updated every hour (or sooner if we have a mitigation).

Immediate asks from our side: if you can share request IDs for a few failed calls (x-redwood-request-id header) that will speed up correlation. We'll also upload a debug bundle shortly.

I'm looping in Vivek (on-call infra) and Marissa and Monica from CS. Expect a triage note within 30 minutes.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden spike in 429/5xx across 11:30-11:50 PT

Forwarding customer reports + sample traces. Sara says DNS lookup failures and large latency/timeout window. Customer traffic shows retry amplification — their clients are aggressively retrying, which is worsening the downstream 429s.

Attachments: perf-logs-20260523.tar.gz, tcpdumps-05-23.pcap (raw captures + spans).

Key context: BrightCart is on a committed Dedicated plan (DEAL-8392) and runs critical checkout flows that must stay under 200ms P95. They want either a configuration mitigation (timeout/backoff tuning + routing) or a temporary region failover.

Can you triage provider dependencies (DNS, upstream network) and confirm whether we had any automated fallback flips in us-west-2? If DNS provider has partial outage, we should consider routing to secondary resolver at infra level and applying short-term retry suppression.

Thanks — need a short write-up we can send to the customer.

—Jonas

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden spike in 429/5xx across 11:30-11:50 PT

Quick triage notes: we've pulled the attached pcap and logs. Initial findings:
- We see increased latency and intermittent TCP RSTs toward one of our egress NAT IP ranges in us-west-2 coincident with DNS timeouts for resolver-1.companydns.com.
- Our autoscaling and health checks did not trigger long-lived node replacement, but several upstream connections aborted and retries from client side increased load, producing transient 429s.
- No model runtime errors in the stacks we control; most client-side failures are at connection and DNS resolution layer.

Immediate actions taken (done):
1) Switched outbound resolver path to secondary resolver pool (resolver-2) for the affected EGRESS subnet (hotfix applied at 09:58 PT).
2) Applied conservative per-customer rate-shedding (soft 10% limit) to break customer retry amplification while we stabilize routing.
3) Increased request timeout at the load-balancer for BrightCart route to reduce upstream aborted requests (short-term trade-off: slightly higher P95 but fewer 5xx).

Next steps:
- Work with DNS provider to confirm incident root cause (we've opened ticket with vendor).
- Monitor metrics for 30–60 minutes; if stable, we roll back rate-shed and restore normal timeouts.
- Prepare post-incident RCA with timeline and remediation (probable: partial resolver outage + aggressive client retries).

I'll publish an incident note to INF-4321 and post updates there. ETA for stabilization: 1–2 hours barring new provider flaps.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden spike in 429/5xx across 11:30-11:50 PT

Thanks for the triage, Vivek. Copying Hannah for visibility (leadership ask).

Customer impact summary for external communications: 
- Impact window: ~11:30–11:50 PT on 2026-05-23
- Observable: elevated 429s and some 5xx; primary symptom was DNS resolution failures leading to higher latencies and client retries
- Mitigation applied: failover to secondary resolver, temporary rate-shed, extended LB timeouts

Customer asks expected: credit for incident window, final RCA, and long-term assurance (secondary resolver SLA or multi-resolver config). Recommend we offer a pro-rated credit and a follow-up technical review with BrightCart to tune client-side backoffs.

I will draft the customer-facing incident note; Jonas, please confirm tone — we should be explicit about the root cause being an upstream DNS provider partial outage while owning our mitigation steps.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 17:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden spike in 429/5xx across 11:30-11:50 PT

Sara —

Thank you for your patience. Quick summary of what happened and our next steps: 

What we saw: between 11:30–11:50 PT you experienced elevated 429s and intermittent 5xxs. Our investigation shows the primary trigger was partial resolution failures to a third-party DNS resolver used by our egress path which produced connection timeouts and amplified retries from clients.

What we did (short-term mitigations):
- Failed over affected egress path to our secondary DNS resolver pool (09:58 PT).
- Applied short-term rate-shedding for BrightCart to reduce retry amplification (10:00 PT).
- Increased LB timeouts for your route to avoid unnecessary aborted requests while we stabilized (10:05 PT).

Status: metrics are returning to baseline after the resolver failover; we've removed most of the temporary rate-shed and are monitoring for 24 hours. Vendor confirmed a partial resolver outage and is performing follow-up work with their network team.

Next steps: 
- We'll share a full RCA and timeline within 48 hours (INF-4321).
- Monica will propose a credit and schedule a technical review to tune client backoffs and discuss making your route resilient to resolver flaps.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the formal RCA and proposed credit. Please let me know if you want immediate handoff to our engineering war room or a call with Monica and Vivek.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
